sources.title: Decreto nº 98.797, de 5 de janeiro de 1990 (Presidency legislation page, archived)
sources.publisher: Presidência da República, Casa Civil, Subchefia para Assuntos Jurídicos
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, seals, coats of arms, signatures, diploma images or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: The Presidency's consolidated legislation page for the decree, captured by the Internet Archive on 24 June 2012; the page states that it does not replace the DOU publication of 8 January 1990. The 2021 capture of Decree No. 98.785 of 4 January 1990 is a bot-check page, so this is the earliest 1990 act of Sarney pinned to a byte-stable response. Live Planalto pages carry a per-request script token and are not byte-stable.

claims.text: Decree No. 98.797 of 5 January 1990, issued by the President of the Republic under Article 84(IV) of the Constitution to revise the values fixed in Decree-Law No. 2.300 of 1986, is dated Brasília 5 January 1990 and signed José Sarney (countersigned João Batista de Abreu); the page notes publication in the DOU of 8 January 1990.

locator.item: heading; preamble 'O PRESIDENTE DA REPÚBLICA'; signature block; note 'Este texto não substitui o publicado no D.O.U. de 8.1.1990'

claims.uncertainty: A signed act attests that Sarney exercised the office on the act's date; it is not a start, an end or a term. The Planalto page is the Presidency's consolidated legislation text, which states that it does not replace the DOU publication. It is the earliest 1990 attestation pinned to a byte-stable response, not the earliest that exists: Decree No. 98.785 of 4 January 1990 (read live) and a Presidency Library speech listed for 4 January 1990 are known, but the archived captures of the decree are bot-check pages and neither is pinned.

sources.publisher: Presidência da República, Casa Civil, Subchefia para Assuntos Jurídicos
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, seals, coats of arms, signatures, diploma images or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: The Presidency's consolidated legislation page, captured 21 February 2015; the page notes the DOU of 14 March 1990. The last archived act of Sarney pinned here; live pages show later acts of 14 March 1990 but are not byte-stable.

claims.text: Decree No. 99.167 of 13 March 1990, issued by the President of the Republic under Article 84(IV) to regulate Law No. 7.976 of 1989 on the federal refinancing of state and municipal external debt, is dated Brasília 13 March 1990 and signed José Sarney (countersigned Mailson Ferreira da Nóbrega); the page notes publication in the DOU of 14 March 1990.

locator.item: heading; preamble; signature block; note 'Este texto não substitui o publicado no D.O.U. de 14.3.1990'

claims.uncertainty: The last archived Sarney signature pinned in this part; it is not his end. The live Planalto pages show later Sarney acts of 14 March 1990 (e.g. Decree No. 99.176) and Collor acts of 15 March 1990 (Decree No. 99.177), not imported because live pages are not byte-stable and no clean capture exists. No primary source read here states the day Sarney's term ended. Context on the role only: it is kept off the holder so that it cannot be read as an end.

sources.title: TSE: Diploma do Presidente da República eleito, Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello (photograph of the diploma)
sources.publisher: Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (Biblioteca Digital da Justiça Eleitoral)
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, seals, coats of arms, signatures, diploma images or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: Photograph (JPEG, 1420x1969) of the diploma in the TSE digital library, item bdtse/1942 (http://bibliotecadigital.tse.jus.br/handle/bdtse/1942); a static bitstream whose ETag equals the MD5 of the bytes (Last-Modified 12 February 2016). The item's catalogue record (https://bibliotecadigital.tse.jus.br/server/api/core/items/25131fb9-9676-49e2-81fc-fadd43f3a79a; 6,656 bytes, SHA-256 5f2621f2e0ff3a11b418902655abc43dafafaaa7f2f451b8537dcf1b7156ac52, stable across two downloads) describes the pictured signed exemplar as an object of the TSE's memory collection acquired by collection ('Coleta') in 1995 and lists unsigned photographic models among related material: it is the TSE's collection exemplar, and nothing here shows it is the exemplar handed to Collor. published_date is the date printed on the diploma.

claims.text: The Superior Electoral Court's diploma, dated Brasília 30 December 1989 and signed by its President, Minister Francisco Rezek, and the other ministers, certifies that Fernando Collor was elected President of the Republic and qualifies him for investiture in the office before the National Congress on 15 March 1990 under the Constitution.

locator.lines: dating line 'Brasília, aos 30 de dezembro de 1989'; body text

claims.uncertainty: The diploma's issue date; the ceremony itself is dated by the TSE catalogue and the 1990 posse record. The investiture day printed on the diploma is prospective and is not a start. The pictured signed exemplar is the TSE's own collection object (catalogue record bdtse/1942: acquired by collection in 1995), not shown to be the exemplar handed to Collor; the printed date is unaffected. Never a holder date.

claims.text: The diploma states that the will of the Brazilian people was expressed at the ballots of 15 November and 17 December 1989, by which Fernando Collor was elected President of the Republic.
claims.uncertainty: Election observation dated by the second (deciding) ballot; the first ballot of 15 November 1989 is in the text. Not a start of office. Never a holder date.

sources.publisher: Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (Biblioteca Digital da Justiça Eleitoral)
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, seals, coats of arms, signatures, diploma images or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: Catalogue record (REST JSON) of the TSE digital library item bdtse/539 (http://bibliotecadigital.tse.jus.br/handle/bdtse/539), a photograph of the 1989 diplomação ceremony; the record's lastModified is 2 April 2020. An archival description, not the minutes of the TSE session.

claims.text: The TSE's catalogue describes the item as the ceremony of diplomação of those elected President and Vice-President of the Republic in the 1989 election, dated 1989-12-30, with Minister Neri da Silveira, Fernando Collor, Minister Francisco Rezek and Itamar Franco present.
claims.uncertainty: Archival catalogue description of a photograph, not the minutes of the TSE session. It agrees with the diploma's date and the 1990 posse record. Never a holder date.

sources.title: Diário do Congresso Nacional nº 8, 16 March 1990: minutes of the 8th joint session of 15 March 1990 (posse)
sources.publisher: Congresso Nacional (printed by the Senado Federal)
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, seals, coats of arms, signatures, diploma images or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: Scanned Diário do Congresso Nacional issue from the Senate's diary store (viewer https://legis.senado.leg.br/diarios/ver/14789).

claims.text: At the solemn joint session of 15 March 1990, after the constitutional oath, the President of the National Congress, Senator Nelson Carneiro, declared Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested ('empossados') as President and Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Nelson Carneiro) - Declaro empossados ...

claims.uncertainty: Posse record with an explicit mandate start of 15 March 1990 (the basis for Collor's from). The Vice-President's posse is the same act and is outside this role.

claims.text: The termo de posse read and signed at the session records that at 10:00 on 15 March 1990, before the National Congress in joint session in the Chamber's plenary, Collor and Itamar Franco were solemnly invested under Article 78 of the Constitution in the offices of President and Vice-President for the period from 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995, and took the prescribed oath.

locator.item: Termo de posse, first paragraph

claims.uncertainty: Same event as the declaration, recorded in the signed termo; the termo's clock time is not relied on.

claims.text: In his address to the joint session of 15 March 1990 Fernando Collor brings to the Legislative Power, before which, following the Constitution, he 'acabo de assumir a Presidência da República' (has just assumed the Presidency of the Republic), his esteem and homage.

locator.item: Collor's address: 'Venho trazer ao Poder Legislativo, ante o qual, seguindo o preceito da Constituição, acabo de assumir a Presidência da República'

claims.uncertainty: The holder's own statement in the Congress record, dated by the session; it supports the declaration and the termo (the basis for from) and gives no clock time. Found by the independent check.

claims.text: The same termo recites that they had been elected in the second round on 17 December of the previous year and certified ('diplomados') by the Superior Electoral Court on 30 December of that year.

locator.item: Termo de posse, 'diplomados, pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, a trinta de dezembro do mesmo ano'

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital of the TSE act, not the TSE's own record; agrees with the diploma. Never a holder date.

claims.text: The session was opened to give posse to the President and Vice-President elected in the second round on 17 December 1989 and certified by the TSE for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: opening statement of the President of Congress

claims.uncertainty: Election recital; never a start or a holder date.

claims.text: Opening the solemn joint session of 15 March 1990, the President of Congress, Senator Nelson Carneiro, stated that it was convened to give posse to the President and Vice-President of the Republic elected in the second round on 17 December 1989 and certified ('diplomados') by the Superior Electoral Court for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995, naming Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Nelson Carneiro) - Declaro aberta a sessão solene ... destinada a dar posse ao Presidente e Vice-Presidente da República

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital of the second-round election; never a start or a holder date. The same passage is already recorded for the President as br_collor_second_round_recited_19891217.

claims.text: After the session resumed (suspended 9:43-9:46), the President and the Vice-President-elect were seated at the Mesa, the Vice-President to the left of the President of the Senate, and both took the constitutional oath ('Prometo manter, defender e cumprir a Constituição ...') before the joint session.

locator.item: 'Os Srs. Presidente e Vice-Presidente da República irão prestar o compromisso constitucional'; the oath text continues on printed page 302

claims.uncertainty: A distinct event recorded before the declaration of posse. The oath is never a start or a holder date (the start rests on the declaration and the termo); no clock time is stored for it.

claims.text: After the oath, the President of Congress declared Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested ('Declaro empossados') as President and Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Nelson Carneiro) - Declaro empossados, para o período de 15 de março de 1990 a 1º de janeiro de 1995, como Presidente e Vice-Presidente ...

claims.uncertainty: Posse record with an explicit period beginning 15 March 1990: the basis for Itamar Franco's from as Vice-President. The printed period end (1 January 1995) is prospective and never an until. The President's posse in the same declaration is br_collor_posse_declared_congress_19900315.

claims.text: The termo de posse read by the First Secretary and signed at the session records that at 10:00 on 15 March 1990, before the National Congress in joint session in the Chamber's plenary, Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco were solemnly invested under Article 78 of the Constitution in the offices of President and Vice-President of the Republic, respectively, for the period 15 March 1990 to 1 January 1995, and took the prescribed oath.

locator.item: Termo de posse dos Excelentíssimos senhores Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello e Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, nos cargos, respectivamente, de Presidente e Vice-Presidente da República

claims.uncertainty: Signed termo of the same posse; supports the declaration. The termo's clock time (10:00) is not relied on (the minutes show the session reopening at 9:46).

claims.text: The same termo recites that the two had been elected in the second round on 17 December of the previous year and certified ('diplomados') by the Superior Electoral Court on 30 December of that year.

locator.item: Termo de posse: 'diplomados, pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, a trinta de dezembro do mesmo ano'

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital of the TSE act; agrees with the TSE diploma (br_itamar_vp_tse_diploma_issued_19891230). Never a holder date.

claims.text: In the Chamber's 145th session of 29 September 1992 (opened at 9:00, closed at 19:32), after the roll call the presiding President of the Chamber, Ibsen Pinheiro, proclaimed 441 votes 'yes', 38 'no', one abstention and 23 absent; the Special Committee's opinion was approved and the accusation against the President of the Republic for crime of responsibility was admitted, the decision to be communicated to the President of the Senate for the purposes of Article 52(I) of the Constitution.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Ibsen Pinheiro) - Encerrada a chamada nominal ...

claims.uncertainty: Authorization to open the process; it does not itself suspend the President or end any term.

claims.text: At the Senate's session of 30 September 1992 the Chamber's Ofício SGM/P nº 1.388, dated 30 September 1992 and signed by its Mesa, was read: the Chamber had resolved at its session of 29 September to authorize the Senate to institute proceedings against President Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello for crime of responsibility, by 441 votes in favour, 38 against, one abstention and 23 absences; the Senate then proceeded to elect the Special Committee.

locator.item: (*) SGM/P nº 1.388 and the President's statement after it

claims.uncertainty: Receipt by the Senate; the Chamber's vote is dated 29 September by the letter itself.

claims.text: At the Senate's session of 1 October 1992 the Senate approved urgency request nº 732/92 and then the opinion (Parecer nº 302, de 1992, dated 30 September) of its Special Committee concluding that the process for crime of responsibility against President Collor should be instituted and that he should be summoned to present his defence; the President of the Senate announced that the Mesa would meet to serve notice on the President and to communicate with the Vice-President, with the President of the Supreme Federal Court to preside over the process.

locator.item: Requerimento nº 732/92; Parecer nº 302, de 1992; continuation on printed page 7902

claims.text: Minutes of the Senate Mesa meeting held at 12:00 on 1 October 1992 with the President of the Supreme Federal Court, Minister Sydney Sanches, to formalize the summons of the President of the Republic and give effect to his removal from the functions of President under Article 86 §2: the summons was approved and signed by the President of the Senate, Mauro Benevides, and by Sanches, who took over the presidency of the process.

locator.item: ATA - MESA, Ata da reunião realizada às 12:00 horas do dia 1º de outubro de 1992 (continues on printed page 790)

claims.uncertainty: Issue of the summons, not its receipt; no suspension is effective on this day.

claims.text: The Mandado de Citação to President Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello, dated Senado Federal 1 October 1992 and signed by Sanches and Benevides, summons him to answer the accusation admitted by the Chamber and states that from receipt of the summons the process is instituted and he is suspended from the functions of President of the Republic under Article 86 §1(II) of the Constitution until the judgment is concluded or the period in §2 elapses.

locator.item: MANDADO DE CITAÇÃO (continues on printed page 788)

claims.uncertainty: The day '1º' in the dating line is partly overwritten by a signature; the Mesa minutes independently date the signing to 1 October.

claims.text: Message SM nº 190/92, dated Senado Federal 1 October 1992 and signed by Sanches and Benevides, informs Vice-President Itamar A. C. Franco that the President has been summoned and in consequence is suspended from his functions until the judgment is concluded or the constitutional period elapses, and that the Vice-President is to assume the Presidency of the Republic immediately under Article 79.

locator.item: SM/nº 190/92 (continues on printed page 789)

claims.uncertainty: Dated before the President's receipt of the summons; it instructs the Vice-President but does not record the time he assumed. Vice-President's exercise: claim only, never a holder.

claims.text: In the contra-fé, signed 'F. Collor' at the Palácio do Planalto on 2 October 1992, Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello acknowledges receiving at 10:20 that day the summons signed by the President of the Supreme Federal Court and the Senate Mesa, presented by the First Secretary, Senator Dirceu Carneiro; under the summons' own terms the process is instituted and the President suspended from his functions from its receipt.

locator.item: CONTRA-FÉ (handwritten time '10.20' and dating line)

claims.uncertainty: The time and the day are handwritten ('às 10.20 horas'; 'Palácio do Planalto, 2 de outubro de 1992'); they were read from renders by the researcher and confirmed by the independent check. The suspension is not an end of Collor's term: he remained the office-holder, suspended, until his resignation.

sources.publisher: Congresso Nacional (printed by the Senado Federal)

claims.text: At the 2nd joint session of 29 December 1992 (opened at 11:30), the President of Congress, Senator Mauro Benevides, stated that at the start of that day's Senate impeachment session defence counsel José Moura Rocha had handed Minister Sydney Sanches a letter by which Collor resigned the mandate, and had the letter read: addressed to the President of the National Congress, dated Brasília 29 December 1992 and signed 'F. Collor', it states that on that date and by that instrument he resigns the mandate of President of the Republic to which he was elected at the ballots of 15 November and 17 December 1989.

locator.item: É LIDA A SEGUINTE CARTA (handwritten facsimile)

claims.uncertainty: The letter is a handwritten facsimile; the reading matches the typeset text in DCN Seção II of 31 December 1992.

claims.text: Immediately after the reading of Collor's letter, the President of Congress ordered its immediate publication in a special edition of the Diário do Congresso Nacional and declared the office of President of the Republic vacant, convening a solemn session for 12:30 that day for the Vice-President's oath; the session rose at 11:50.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Mauro Benevides) - ... declaro vago o cargo de Presidente da República

claims.uncertainty: Declaration of vacancy by the President of Congress; together with the letter and the termo below it supports Collor's until.

claims.text: At the solemn 3rd joint session of 29 December 1992 (opened at 12:30), after Itamar Franco took the constitutional oath, the President of Congress declared Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested ('empossado') as President of the Federative Republic of Brazil for the period 29 December 1992 to 1 January 1995.

locator.item: O SR. PRESIDENTE (Mauro Benevides) - Declaro, com profunda emoção, empossado ...

claims.uncertainty: Posse record with an explicit mandate start of 29 December 1992 (the basis for Itamar Franco's from). The printed end of the period is prospective and is not used.

claims.text: The termo de posse records that at 12:30 on 29 December 1992, before the National Congress in joint session, Vice-President Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, elected in the second round of 17 December 1989, appeared to be invested under Article 79 of the Constitution in the office of President of the Republic by virtue of the resignation of Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello 'ocorrida nesta data' (which occurred on that date), and took the oath under Article 78.

locator.item: Termo de posse do Exmº Sr. Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco

claims.uncertainty: Signed termo of the same posse; its statement that the resignation occurred that day is also recorded as a separate claim for Collor.

claims.text: The same termo states that the office was filled by virtue of Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello's resignation, which occurred on 29 December 1992.

locator.item: Termo de posse, 'em virtude da renúncia ... ocorrida nesta data'

claims.uncertainty: States the day of the resignation, not a clock time. The letter was presented to the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 (br_collor_resignation_letter_read_senate_19921229) and read in Congress between 11:30 and 11:50; no source states the hour it took effect.

claims.text: Itamar Franco's handwritten declaration to the President of Congress, dated Brasília 29 December 1992 and published in the minutes, states that his declaration of assets that day is the same one he presented on 2 October of that year, when he assumed, as Vice-President, the exercise of the office of President of the Republic.

locator.item: É a seguinte a declaração recebida (handwritten)

claims.uncertainty: Retrospective statement by the Vice-President himself, handwritten; the reading 'em dia 2 de outubro do corrente ano, quando assumi a condição de Vice-Presidente em exercício do cargo de Presidente da República' was made from renders and confirmed by the independent check. Vice-President's exercise: claim only, never a holder or a start.

claims.text: At the 2nd joint session of 29 December 1992 (11:30-11:50), after Collor's letter was read and the office of President declared vacant, the President of Congress, Senator Mauro Benevides, said that in consequence he would inform the Vice-President of the Republic, Dr. Itamar Franco, that he must appear before Congress at 12:30 that day to take the oath as President of the Republic.

locator.item: 'Em conseqüência da vacância agora proclamada, irei cientificar o Vice-Presidente da República, Dr. Itamar Franco, de que deve comparecer hoje ao Congresso Nacional, às 12h30min'

claims.uncertainty: The President of Congress announces that he will notify the Vice-President ('irei cientificar'); the notification itself is not recorded in the issue. It styles Itamar Franco as Vice-President on 29 December 1992, before his posse as President. The vacancy it follows is that of the office of President (CLAUDE-C01-10's br_presidency_vacancy_declared_19921229, which is not cited on this role); it says nothing of the office of Vice-President, sets no end and states no vacancy of the Vice-Presidency.

claims.text: The termo de posse records that at 12:30 on 29 December 1992 Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, Vice-President of the Republic, elected in the second round on 17 December 1989, appeared before the National Congress in joint session to be invested, under Article 79 of the Constitution, in the office of President of the Republic by virtue of the resignation of Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello that day, and took the oath under Article 78.

locator.item: Termo de posse do Exmo Sr. Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco no cargo de Presidente da República: 'compareceu o Sr. Dr. Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco, Vice-Presidente da República ... a fim de ser investido, de acordo com o art. 79 ...'

claims.uncertainty: The Vice-President's succession to the Presidency (his posse as President is CLAUDE-C01-10's br_itamar_posse_declared_congress_19921229 and br_itamar_termo_de_posse_19921229 on br_president). The record neither declares the office of Vice-President vacant nor states that his vice-presidential office ended, so it sets no until and no vacancy on br_vice_president; his posse as President is never an end of his vice-presidential office, and nothing is inferred from it.

sources.publisher: Senado Federal

sources.scope_note: Scanned Seção II (Órgão Judiciário) issue of Wednesday 30 December 1992 (Ano XLVII, nº 32), archived by the Senate as the Suplemento Único to DSF nº 223/1992 (viewer https://legis.senado.leg.br/diarios/ver/20356; printed pages 2727-3018 in 328 PDF pages; built with iText 2.1.7, CreationDate 22 April 2016). Located by the independent check, which downloaded it three times: the first transfer came back 1,390 bytes short and was discarded, and the other two were identical. A large Senate PDF that mismatches once should be fetched again before it is called unstable.

claims.text: The supplement, dated Wednesday 30 December 1992, opens with Resolução nº 101, de 1992, promulgated by Mauro Benevides as President of the Senate and dated Senado Federal 30 December 1992: it declares the request for loss of office prejudiced by Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello's resignation, formalized before the National Congress, upholds the accusation, imposes on him disqualification ('inabilitação') for eight years from exercising public functions, and enters into force on the date of its publication.

locator.item: RESOLUÇÃO Nº 101, DE 1992, arts. 1-4 and dating line

claims.uncertainty: The resolution's first printing; DSF nº 224 of 31 December 1992 (br_senate_resolution_101_disqualification_19921230) is a reprint. In force on publication (30 December 1992). It mentions no political rights and bounds no holder. Located by the independent check.

claims.text: At the Senate's session as a court on 29 December 1992 (opened at 9:00), defence counsel José Moura Rocha said he had just spoken by telephone with the suspended President Fernando Collor de Mello and read to the Senate Collor's letter to the President of the National Congress, dated Brasília 29 December 1992 and signed 'F. Collor', stating that on that date and by that instrument he resigns the mandate of President of the Republic. The President of Congress, Mauro Benevides, then convened a joint session for 11:30 that day, and Minister Sydney Sanches suspended the Senate session at 9:43 so that Congress could receive the resignation and declare the vacancy; it reopened at 13:40.

locator.item: attendance at 9:00 (p. 2729); Moura Rocha's reading of the letter, with its handwritten facsimile (p. 2738); Benevides's convocation (p. 2741); 'Suspensa às 9h43min, a sessão é reaberta às 13h40min' (p. 2742)

claims.uncertainty: Places the letter's presentation to the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 on 29 December; the letter itself states the day, not a time. Congress read it and declared the vacancy between 11:30 and 11:50 (br_collor_resignation_letter_read_congress_19921229). Supports Collor's end, which stays day-only. Located by the independent check.

claims.text: When the session resumed, the Senate voted on whether the process should continue after the resignation: the panel printout headed '29.12.92 18:17 HORAS', 'PROSSEGUIMENTO DO PROCESSO DE IMPEACHMENT', shows 71 yes and 8 no; Sanches declared that the Senate had decided by 71 votes to 8 that the process against Collor should continue to consider the sanction of disqualification ('inabilitação'), and after two senators declared votes not registered on the panel he proclaimed 73 yes and 8 no.

locator.item: vote panel '29.12.92 18:17 HORAS 2.SESSAO 1.VOTACAO'; the proclamations by Sydney Sanches

claims.uncertainty: A procedural vote after the resignation; it concerns only the disqualification sanction and neither ends nor extends Collor's term. The panel prints 79 votes; the proclaimed total of 81 includes the two declared votes. Located by the independent check.

claims.text: The panel printout headed '30.12.92 04:21 HORAS', 'INABILITACAO POR OITO ANOS', records 76 yes, 3 no and no abstentions (total 79); Sanches announced the result, noting that abstention was not permitted, and read the sentence against Collor. The session rose at 4:40 on the following day, 30 December 1992.

locator.item: vote panel '30.12.92 04:21 HORAS 2.SESSAO 2.VOTACAO'; announcement of the result; closing line on PDF page 324 'Levanta-se a sessão às 4h40min do dia imediato'

claims.uncertainty: The vote on the eight-year disqualification ('inabilitação ... para o exercício de função pública'); it is not a loss of political rights and does not bound Collor's term, which ended with the resignation on 29 December. Located by the independent check.

Collor', by which, on that date and by that instrument, he resigns the mandate of President of the Republic for which he was elected at the ballots of 15 November and 17 December 1989.

locator.item: CONGRESSO NACIONAL box

claims.uncertainty: Typeset reprint of the letter read in Congress on 29 December.

claims.text: The Senate's sentence as judicial body, dated Brasília 30 December 1992 and signed by Minister Sydney Sanches and the senators, recites that the session was suspended so that Congress could receive the resignation and declare the vacancy; that, the presidential mandate having been extinguished by the resignation, the process ended as to removal from office; and that, the two-thirds quorum having been reached, the Senate condemned him to disqualification ('inabilitação') for eight years from exercising public functions under Article 52, sole paragraph.

locator.item: SENADO FEDERAL COMO ÓRGÃO JUDICIÁRIO - SENTENÇA, items 1-5; items 6-11 and dating line on printed page 11172

claims.uncertainty: Judgment after the resignation; it states that the mandate was extinguished by the resignation and does not remove him from office. The session minutes date the disqualification vote to 04:21 on 30 December (br_senate_disqualification_vote_19921230). Never a boundary.

claims.text: Resolução nº 101, de 1992, promulgated by the President of the Senate, Mauro Benevides, and dated Senado Federal 30 December 1992, declares the request for the sanction of loss of office prejudiced by the resignation presented and formalized before the National Congress, upholds the accusation of crimes of responsibility, imposes on Fernando Affonso Collor de Mello disqualification for eight years from exercising public functions, and enters into force on publication.

locator.item: RESOLUÇÃO Nº 101, DE 1992, arts. 1-4

claims.uncertainty: The resolution's date. Its first printing is the Suplemento Único to DSF nº 223 dated 30 December 1992 (br_senate_resolution_101_first_printed_19921230), which puts its entry into force on 30 December; this 31 December issue is a reprint. The Senate matter page also lists the DOU of 31 December 1992, page 18979, whose viewer requires a CAPTCHA and was not read. The resolution imposes disqualification from public functions ('inabilitação') and does not mention political rights ('direitos políticos'). Never a boundary.

claims.text: Opening the 69th joint session of 22 April 1985, the President of Congress, Senator José Fragelli, recalled that the Vice-President, José Sarney, had taken the constitutional oath before the National Congress on 15 March 1985.

locator.item: 'ao Vice-Presidente, sua Excelência o Senhor Doutor José Sarney, que já prestou, perante o Congresso Nacional, a 15 de março do corrente ano, o compromisso constitucional'

claims.uncertainty: Congress's recital, dated by the day recalled; outside the 1990-2026 window. The oath is never a start or a holder date, and no holder is recorded for José Sarney as Vice-President.

claims.text: The same statement says that the Vice-President had since then been in the exercise of the Presidency by reason of the impediment of the holder (the President-elect).

locator.item: 'encontra-se, desde então, no exercício da Presidência em virtude do impedimento do titular'

claims.uncertainty: Recited on 22 April 1985 as running since the oath of 15 March 1985, and dated by the day recalled, as CLAUDE-C01-10 dates Itamar Franco's own statement. The source states no day on which the exercise as Vice-President ended, and Mensagem nº 232 of 21 April already has him continuing as successor, so no period is stored. Exercise of the Presidency: a claim only, never a holder, and outside the window.

claims.text: He stated that, President-elect Tancredo de Almeida Neves having died, the office of President of the Republic being vacant, it fell to the Vice-President, José Sarney, as successor of the President-elect, to exercise the office of President of the Republic under Article 77, caput, of the Constitution.

locator.item: summary 'vacância do cargo de Presidente da República; e assunção do Doutor José Sarney ao cargo de Presidente da República'; 'Vago o cargo de Presidente da República, ao Vice-Presidente ... cabe exercer, como sucessor ...'

claims.uncertainty: Declares the vacancy of the office of President, not of the Vice-Presidency. No source reviewed states that the office of Vice-President was vacant, in 1985 or on 1 January 1990; nothing is inferred from this succession about the office on 1 January 1990.

claims.text: Mensagem nº 232, dated Brasília 21 April 1985, signed José Sarney and read at the session, informs the President of the Senate of the death that day of President-elect Tancredo de Almeida Neves and states that Sarney continues to exercise, now as successor, the office of President of the Republic under Article 77 of the Constitution.

locator.item: MENSAGEM Nº 232: 'continuo a exercer, agora na qualidade de sucessor, o cargo de Presidente da República'

claims.uncertainty: The successor's own statement; it does not mention the office of Vice-President. Context for BR-VP-01 only.

claims.text: The profile of José Sarney gives his period as Vice-President as 15/03/1985 to 21/04/1985, with Tancredo de Almeida Neves as President, and says that Tancredo died before taking office and Sarney assumed the office on 21 April 1985.

roles.title: Presidente Nacional do Partido dos Trabalhadores

holder_claims.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
holder_claims.note: From 3 June 1990: in his closing speech to the VII Encontro Nacional, printed by the party's Boletim Nacional nº 51, Lula says 'Volto a assumir a Presidência do Partido dos Trabalhadores' and that he receives the baton from Luiz Gushiken 'hoje' (Sunday 3 June 1990); the standfirst calls him 'reconduzido à presidência do PT'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no party record states the day or the reason his presidency ended in 1994; the bulletin still calls him 'o presidente do PT' in the first fortnight of April 1994, and Rui Falcão's styling as Presidente Nacional from the second fortnight of May 1994 is not used as his end. The VII Encontro's election (31 May-3 June 1990) and the executive committee's election of 15 July 1990 are separate claims. If a speech is not accepted as a stated assumption, the fallback is attested_on 1990-06-03. Luiz Gushiken, president when the period opens, has no holder: no record gives a single day of his presidency.

holder_claims.name: Rui Falcão
holder_claims.note: Observed on 25 November 1994: the PT's special edition of the Boletim Nacional (Dezembro/94) says 'O presidente nacional do PT, deputado Rui Falcão, abriu o Seminário' held that day.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: no party record states when or how he took the office or whether his service was interim (Boletim Nacional nº 85 calls him a vice-president in the first fortnight of April 1994; nº 87 and nº 91 style him Presidente Nacional in May and October 1994 without a day). No end: who led the party from December 1994 to August 1995 is unresolved, and José Dirceu's election at the 10th Encontro (18-20 August 1995) is not used as his end. The PT's December 2002 count of its presidents omits him; the party's portal of 2011 ('já foi presidente do partido') and its 2017 biography ('em 1994, presidente do PT Nacional') count him.

holder_claims.name: José Dirceu
holder_claims.note: Observed on 24 August 1995: the ofício nº 001/95 of the PT's Secretaria Nacional de Combate ao Racismo is addressed 'Ao Sr. José Dirceu, Presidente do Diretório Nacional'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the 10th Encontro's vote (215 to 183, day not printed) and the directorate lists are election claims, and no source states the day he assumed the office. No end: his re-election at the 11th Encontro (August 1997) begins a new observation and is not an end.

holder_claims.name: José Dirceu
holder_claims.note: Observed on 17 September 1997: PT Notícias nº 52 reports that 'o presidente nacional do PT, José Dirceu' took part in the meeting held in Vitória 'No dia 17'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the vote of 31 August 1997 (284 to 256) and the undated proclamation are election claims, never a start; the earlier proposal to date this holder by the vote day was withdrawn after the independent check. No end.

holder_claims.name: José Dirceu
holder_claims.note: Observed on 2 December 1999: a letter of the national presidency is signed 'José Dirceu, Presidente Nacional do Partido dos Trabalhadores'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the result was known on 28 November 1999 and he 'assumed his third term during the II Congresso' (24-28 November) with no day printed. No end: his leave of 17 July 2001 to stand in the direct election and José Genoino's acting service (July to October 2001) are claims only and neither end nor split this holder.

holder_claims.name: José Dirceu
holder_claims.note: Observed on 4 October 2001: an official note dated 'São Paulo, 4 de outubro de 2001' is signed 'Deputado federal José Dirceu (PT-SP), presidente nacional do PT' (PT Notícias nº 109).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the totalisation of 27 September 2001 is a result declaration, and his stated resumption of 1 October 2001 follows a leave. The same issue's masthead still lists José Genoino '(em exercício)', recorded as an acting-service claim (probably stale, but the source does not say so). No end: on 7 December 2002 he took leave and José Genoino replaced him on an interim basis; he resigned at the Diretório Nacional meeting of 15-16 March 2003, a two-day meeting with no single day, so no until is recorded.

holder_claims.name: José Genoino
holder_claims.note: Observed on 18 March 2003: the Portal do PT reports a ceremony attended by 'o presidente do PT, José Genoino' and quotes 'O presidente nacional do PT'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the Diretório Nacional elected him on 15 March 2003 (an election claim), and the party compilation records his service from 7 December 2002 to 15 March 2003 as interim, so the portal's stylings of 8 and 13 January 2003 are claims only. No end: his declaration of 9 July 2005 hands the office to the Diretório Nacional and calls it a leave, no act accepting a resignation or declaring a vacancy was found, and Tarso Genro's selection that night is not used as his end.

holder_claims.name: Tarso Genro
holder_claims.note: Observed on 10 July 2005: the Portal do PT reports the national executive committee's decisions 'segundo informou o presidente Tarso Genro'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the Diretório Nacional approved his name on 9 July 2005 (a selection claim), the report's 'novos empossados' names nobody and records no posse, and the selection day is kept out of holder dates. No PT record calls him interim (Berzoini's 2010 speech recalls leading the party 'primeiro interinamente' in 2005, a retrospective claim). No end: the last dated styling is of 14 October 2005, and Ricardo Berzoini's posse of 22 October 2005 is not used as his end.

holder_claims.name: Ricardo Berzoini
holder_claims.note: From 22 October 2005: the Portal do PT reports that 'O Diretório Nacional deu posse, neste sábado (22), ao presidente eleito, Ricardo Berzoini', and lists 'Presidência - Ricardo Berzoini' in the new executive committee.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: Marco Aurélio Garcia's listing as 'Presidente (interino)' (November 2006 to January 2007) is claims only and neither splits nor ends this holder; the PED 2007 begins a new observation. The PED 2005 ballots (18 September and 9 October) and result declarations (11 and 13 October 2005) are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Ricardo Berzoini
holder_claims.note: Observed on 13 November 2009 (the capture date of an undated page): the Portal do PT's page 'Integrantes da CEN para o biênio 2008/2009' lists 'Ricardo Berzoini - Presidente'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: no PT record of the PED 2007 result or of a 2008 posse was found (a deputy's aside of 2010 gives him terms '2005 a 2007 e de 2007 a 2010', a retrospective claim), and the printed biennium is not a boundary. No end: his statement in Congress that 10 February 2010 was 'o último dia do meu mandato' conflicts with the PT's report that he 'deixa a presidência' at José Eduardo Dutra's posse on 19 February 2010; both are claims only, and Dutra's posse is not used as his end.

holder_claims.name: José Eduardo Dutra
holder_claims.note: From 19 February 2010: the Portal do PT reports that on the night of Friday 19 February 2010 'foram empossados o novo presidente José Eduardo Dutra' and the new Diretório Nacional. Until 29 April 2011: the Portal do PT's item of 8 May 2011 says 'A renúncia do presidente do PT José Eduardo Dutra no dia 29 de abril'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end rests on the party's statement of the day of his resignation (the year from the item's date); the day of the Diretório Nacional meeting that elected Rui Falcão (29 or 30 April 2011) is not used. The PED 2009 declaration (25 November 2009), final result (2 December 2009) and the rule setting the posse for 20 February 2010 are separate claims; Rui Falcão's acting service in April 2011 is a claim only.

holder_claims.name: Rui Falcão
holder_claims.note: Observed on 8 May 2011: the Portal do PT quotes the secretary-general on 'o novo presidente nacional do PT, Rui Falcão'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: his election by the Diretório Nacional by unanimity is reported without a day, and the PT's own article on it has no usable capture; his acting service of 26 April 2011 is a claim only. No end: the PED 2013 re-election begins a new observation.

holder_claims.name: Rui Falcão
holder_claims.note: Observed on 18 December 2013: the Portal do PT lists the national leaders 'empossado durante o 5º Congresso', headed 'Rui Goethe da Costa Falcão, Presidente'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the PED 2013 vote (10 November) and announcement (12 November) are election claims; the posse took place during the 5th Congress and was scheduled for the night of 12 December 2013, but no source reports the day it took place (the posse speech was published on 12 December). No end: no source states the day his presidency ended; Gleisi Hoffmann's election (3 June 2017) and posse (5 July 2017), the retrospective 'maio de 2017' and the TSE registry periods (to 8 September and 9 October 2017) are not used. The 2015 re-election in the work order's hint is not supported.

holder_claims.name: Gleisi Hoffmann
holder_claims.note: From 5 July 2017: the PT reports that the new Diretório Nacional 'está sendo empossado hoje' with the new presidenta, Gleisi Hoffmann (in a post dated Wednesday 5 July 2017), and a same-day report speaks of the posse of 'the new presidenta of the PT, Gleisi Hoffmann'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: her re-election at the 7th Congress (24 November 2019) begins a new observation. Her election by the 6th Congress on 3 June 2017 is a claim only.

holder_claims.name: Gleisi Hoffmann
holder_claims.note: Observed on 1 April 2020 (the capture date of an undated page): the PT's Diretório Nacional page heads its list 'Presidenta Nacional do PT - Gleisi Hoffmann - Paraná'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: no posse day of the 2019 term was found. No end: on 7 March 2025 the PT announced her departure and the executive named Humberto Costa for the interim command, and the Diretório page cites her resignation as the reason, but no source states the day her office ended (the PT's pages of 13 and 20 March 2025 say Humberto Costa took over early in the following week); the TSE registry's exercise end of 07/03/2025 is a registry period. Her ministerial post is state office and ends nothing here.

holder_claims.name: Humberto Costa
holder_claims.note: From 20 March 2025: after the Diretório Nacional ratified his choice that day, Humberto Costa said 'agora saio da condição de presidente interino para presidente efetivo' (pt.org.br, 20 March 2025).
holder_claims.uncertainty: His service from 7 to 19 March 2025 is interim (the executive's designation, the Diretório page and the PT pages of 12 and 13 March), claims only. The start rests on his own statement of that day; Codex may prefer attested_on 2025-03-20. The Diretório Nacional's election of that day (63-0-5) is a separate claim. No end: Edinho Silva's posse of 3 August 2025 is not used as his end, and the TSE registry's end (23/08/2025) is the organ's.

holder_claims.name: Edinho Silva
holder_claims.note: From 3 August 2025: the PT states that Edinho Silva was 'empossado neste domingo (3)' at the close of the 17th Encontro Nacional.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The same day's 13h27 page announced that he 'assume oficialmente o cargo na próxima segunda-feira (4)'; that statement is prospective and unconfirmed and is recorded as a claim. If Codex prefers it, the fallback is attested_on 2025-09-17 (the Diretório page), never 4 August. The PED vote (6 July), the partial result (7 July), the totalization (15 July) and the president-elect styling (16 July) are separate claims, and the TSE registry's 23 August 2025 is a registry period. No end is stated before the cutoff.

holder_claims.name: Edinho Silva
holder_claims.note: Observed on 15 August 2026 (the capture date of an undated page): the PT's Diretório Nacional page heads its list 'Presidente Nacional do PT - Edinho Silva - São Paulo'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the latest attestation before the cutoff, a second observation of the term begun on 3 August 2025. The TSE's live SGIP record of the current national organ (last altered 8 July 2026) also lists him as PRESIDENTE, Ativo, but it is a lead: the record is in force and will change on its next annotation.

roles.scope_note: Presidente Nacional do Partido dos Trabalhadores, the party office, recorded on the PT's 2024 funding observation (whose identity, lifecycle and empty game mapping are unchanged). CLAUDE-C01-22 keeps national meetings (Encontros and Congressos), direct elections (PED) with their ballots, counts and declarations, Diretório Nacional selections, the assumption of the office (posse), resignations and leaves, interim and acting arrangements and in-office attestations as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a source states the day the office was assumed or took effect (a reported posse or the holder's stated assumption), and an end only where a source states the day it ended (José Eduardo Dutra's resignation of 29 April 2011 is the only one); otherwise it is dated by attested_on from an in-office attestation of that day. Acting, interim and continuation service are claims only, never holders, and never split or end a holder. Do not fill the interval between observations or infer an outgoing holder's last day from a successor's election or posse. Party office and the Presidency of the Republic stay separate: no br_presidency claim or source feeds this role, and none of its claims feeds br_presidency; state offices never start, end or split a holder. Retrospective lists, counts, biographies and registry exercise periods are claims, never boundaries; party statutes and PED regulations are procedure only, never a date. Holder names are normalised and the printed forms stay in the claim texts; every claim and source id of this role begins br_pt_.

PT national presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-22): role br_pt_president holds eighteen holder observations from party, Chamber and electoral-court records (stated starts for Lula 1990, Ricardo Berzoini 2005, José Eduardo Dutra 2010, Gleisi Hoffmann 2017, Humberto Costa 2025 and Edinho Silva 2025; one stated end, Dutra's resignation of 29 April 2011). Still open: the day Lula's presidency ended in 1994 and whether Rui Falcão's 1994 service was interim; who led the party from December 1994 to August 1995; the day of José Genoino's designation in December 2002 and of José Dirceu's resignation (a meeting of 15-16 March 2003); whether Genoino's act of 9 July 2005 was a resignation or a leave and whether Tarso Genro's presidency was interim; the PED 2007 result; the day every other term ended; and Edinho Silva's contested assumption day (3 or 4 August 2025). roles.title: President of the Federative Republic of Brazil

holder_claims.name: José Sarney
holder_claims.note: Observed on 5 January 1990, signing Decree No. 98.797 as President (the Presidency's archived legislation page): the earliest 1990 attestation pinned to a byte-stable response. He also signed Decree No. 99.167 on 13 March 1990; that act is a claim on the role, not a holder date.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: his 1985 assumption lies outside the packet period. No end: no primary source reviewed states the day his term ended; the Presidency Library's retrospective span (15.03.1985-15.03.1990) is a claim only, the Constitution's transitional provision is procedure only, and Collor's posse of 15 March 1990 is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Fernando Collor de Mello
holder_claims.note: From 15 March 1990: the President of Congress declared him invested for the period beginning that day, and the termo records the posse at 10:00 (DCN nº 8/1990); in his address he says he has just assumed the Presidency. Until 29 December 1992: his letter resigns the mandate 'nesta data e por este instrumento', the President of Congress declared the office vacant that day, and Itamar Franco's termo de posse states that the resignation occurred that day; the letter was also read to the Senate that morning.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is day-only: the letter reached the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 and was read in Congress between 11:30 and 11:50, and no source states the hour of effect. He was suspended from 2 October 1992 on receiving the summons (a claim); the suspension is not an end and the holder is not split. The TSE diploma (30 December 1989) and the ballots of 15 November and 17 December 1989 are separate claims. The judgment of 30 December 1992 and Resolução nº 101 (disqualification for eight years) follow the resignation and bound nothing.

holder_claims.name: Itamar Franco
holder_claims.note: From 29 December 1992: declared invested as President for the period beginning that day, and the termo records the posse at 12:30 by virtue of Collor's resignation that day (DCN nº 70/1992).
holder_claims.uncertainty: His exercise of the office as Vice-President from 2 October 1992 (his own statement; Law No. 8.471) is recorded only as claims, never as this holder or its start. No end: the only statement is Fernando Henrique Cardoso's thanks in his 1 January 1995 posse address ('No momento em que deixa o Governo'), a successor's statement recorded as a claim, not a boundary; the printed period end is prospective, and Cardoso's posse is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Fernando Henrique Cardoso
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 1995: declared invested for the period beginning that day, and the termo records the solemn posse (DCN nº 1/1995); in his address he speaks of the position 'que assumo hoje'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the stated period end (31 December 1998) is prospective, and the Congress President's 1999 reference to 'o mandato que se findou' gives no day. The oath before Congress, the 3 October 1994 election and the 17 December 1994 diplomação are separate claims and never boundaries.

holder_claims.name: Fernando Henrique Cardoso
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 1999: declared invested for the second mandate beginning that day ('a iniciar-se nesta data'), and the termo records the posse at 17:00 (DCN nº 1/1999); the Congress President speaks of the mandate 'que hoje se inicia'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the period end printed at the posse (31 December 2002) is prospective, and the 2003 Congress record does not name him. No record of the 2003 sash transfer is imported (the Senate agency's report is a lead).

holder_claims.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2003: declared invested for the period beginning that day, and the signed termo records the posse (DCN nº 1/2003); the First Secretary said he 'hoje assume a Presidência', and in 2007 Lula recalled assuming the Presidency in that chamber on a 1 January four years earlier.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2006) is prospective and the end of the first term is not dated. The oath, the 27 October 2002 election and the 14 December 2002 diplomação are separate claims. The termo's clock time (15:00) precedes the recorded session opening (15:05) and is not used.

holder_claims.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2007: declared invested for the new mandate beginning that day, and the signed termo records the posse (DCN nº 1/2007); he speaks of 'this inaugural day of my new mandate'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end. Dilma Rousseff's Parlatório address of 1 January 2011 says 'Hoje o presidente Lula deixa o governo', a successor's statement recorded as a claim and not used as a boundary; the printed period end (31 December 2010) is prospective and differs from it by a day; Rousseff's posse is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Dilma Rousseff
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2011: declared invested for the period beginning that day, and the signed termo records the posse (DCN nº 1/2011); the President of Congress told her that through the commitment the President-elect assumes the responsibility, and in her Parlatório address she says 'eu assumo hoje o governo do meu país'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2014) is prospective. Her statement in Congress that the sash would be placed on her 'today' is prospective and a claim only; no record of the transfer itself is imported.

holder_claims.name: Dilma Rousseff
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2015: declared invested for the period beginning that day, and the signed termo records the posse (DCN nº 1/2015); in her Parlatório address she says 'Assumo meu segundo mandato'. Until 31 August 2016: the Senate's Resolution No. 35 of that day imposes loss of office and enters into force on publication, and the DOU extra edition of 31 August 2016 publishes it.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The end is day-only; no hour of effect is printed. Michel Temer's termo de posse also states that the vacancy occurred on 31 August 2016 (cited by his holder). She was suspended from 12 May 2016 on receiving the intimation (a claim); the suspension is not an end and the holder is not split. The printed period end (31 December 2018), the Chamber's authorization, the Senate's admission, the judgment votes and the separate disqualification vote (not imposed) are claims, never boundaries.

holder_claims.name: Michel Temer
holder_claims.note: From 31 August 2016: declared invested for the period beginning that day 'tendo em vista a vacância do cargo', and the signed termo records the posse by virtue of the vacancy that occurred on 31 August 2016 (DCN nº 15/2016).
holder_claims.uncertainty: His exercise as Vice-President from 12 May 2016 (MP 726 and later acts) is recorded only as claims, never as this holder or its start. No end: the printed period end (31 December 2018) is prospective, the Congress President's 'ex-Presidente' styling on 1 January 2019 is context, and Bolsonaro's posse is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Jair Bolsonaro
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2019: declared invested for the period beginning that day, and the signed termo records the posse at 15:00 (DCN nº 1/2019); he signed MP 870 as President the same day.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2022) is prospective; Vice-President Mourão's exercise of the office on 30 and 31 December 2022 is recorded only as claims; Lula's posse is not used as this end. The 1 January 2019 sash ceremony is a claim with a misprinted dateline that names no giver. The 28 October 2018 election and the 10 December 2018 diplomação are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2023: declared invested for the period beginning that day (DCN nº 1/2023); he signed MP 1.154 as President the same day, and MP 1.388 as President on 24 August 2026, before the cutoff.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (4 January 2027) falls after the 7 September 2026 cutoff and is kept in claim text only; the 2026 attestation does not extend the term. The 30 October 2022 election and the 12 December 2022 diplomação are separate claims; no sash record of 1 January 2023 was found.

roles.scope_note: President of the Federative Republic of Brazil under the 1988 Constitution, recorded here as head of state (the office is also head of government). CLAUDE-C01-10 keeps popular election, diplomação by the Superior Electoral Court, the oath before Congress, the declaration of posse, the termo de posse, assumption statements, sash ceremonies, the Chamber's authorization, the Senate's admission, the summons and its receipt (suspension), the Vice-President's exercise of the office, resignation, vacancy, the Senate's judgment, removal and disqualification as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a declaration of posse or a termo de posse states that the person was invested for a period beginning that day, and an end only where a source states the day a resignation or removal took effect; otherwise it is dated by attested_on. Oaths, elections, diplomações and sash ceremonies are never boundaries; periods declared at a posse are prospective and never ends; a successor's or third party's statement that the predecessor leaves office is a claim only; retrospective Presidency Library spans are claims with no structured date. A Vice-President exercising the office (Itamar Franco in 1992, Michel Temer in 2016, Hamilton Mourão in 2022) is recorded as claims, never as a holder of it. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. Vice-presidents, ministers and party offices are otherwise outside this role.

roles.title: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil

holder_claims.name: Itamar Franco
holder_claims.note: From 15 March 1990: the President of Congress declared Collor and Itamar Augusto Cautiero Franco invested as President and Vice-President 'para o período de 15 de março de 1990 a 1º de janeiro de 1995', and the signed termo records their posse under Article 78 (DCN nº 8/1990).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no reviewed source states the day his vice-presidential office ended or that the office became vacant. His exercise of the Presidency (11 December 1991; from 2 October 1992) is recorded only as claims, and his posse as President on 29 December 1992, the vacancy of the office of President declared that day, the printed period end (1 January 1995) and the retrospective 29/12/1992 spans are not used as this end. The 17 December 1989 election, the 30 December 1989 diplomação and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Marco Maciel
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 1995: declared invested as Vice-President for the period beginning that day, and the joint termo records the solemn posse (DCN nº 1/1995); the President of Congress saluted him as Vice-President at the close.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 1998) is prospective and no reviewed source states the day the term ended; his styling as Vice-President at the opening of the 1999 session is a claim only, and his 1999 posse is not used as this end. The 3 October 1994 election, the 17 December 1994 diplomação (Congress record and TSE diploma) and the oath are separate claims and never boundaries.

holder_claims.name: Marco Maciel
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 1999: declared invested as Vice-President for the second mandate beginning that day ('a iniciar-se nesta data'), and the termo records the posse (DCN nº 1/1999).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2002) is prospective, the 2003 Congress record does not name him, and Alencar's posse is not used as this end. The 4 October 1998 re-election, the 12 December 1998 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: José Alencar
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2003: declared invested as Vice-President for the period beginning that day, and the signed termo records the posse (DCN nº 1/2003).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2006) is prospective; his styling at the opening of the 2007 session is a claim only, and his 2007 posse is not used as this end. The 27 October 2002 election, the 14 December 2002 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: José Alencar
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2007: declared invested as Vice-President for the period beginning that day, with the signed termo de compromisso and termo de posse (DCN nº 1/2007).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2010) is prospective; Rousseff's 1 January 2011 tribute (br_alencar_tribute_rousseff_address_20110101) is a successor administration's statement with no day, a claim only and never a boundary; Temer's posse is not used as this end. The 29 October 2006 re-election, the 14 December 2006 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Michel Temer
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2011: declared invested as Vice-President for the period beginning that day, with the signed termo de compromisso and termo de posse (DCN nº 1/2011).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2014) is prospective, no reviewed source states the day the term ended, and his 2015 posse is not used as this end. The 31 October 2010 election, the 17 December 2010 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Michel Temer
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2015: declared invested as Vice-President for the period beginning that day, with the signed termo de compromisso and termo de posse (DCN nº 1/2015).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2018) is prospective. His notification and interim exercise of the Presidency from 12 May 2016 are claims only and neither split nor end this holder, and his posse as President on 31 August 2016 (by virtue of the vacancy of the office of President) states no end of the Vice-Presidency and no vacancy of it; the retrospective 31/08/2016 span and chronology are claims only, and Mourão's posse is not used as this end. His br_president holder (CLAUDE-C01-10, from 31 August 2016) is unchanged. The 26 October 2014 election, the 18 December 2014 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Hamilton Mourão
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2019: declared invested as Vice-President for the period beginning that day ('para o período a iniciar-se nesta data'), with the termo read into the record and the signed joint termo de posse at 15:00 (DCN nº 1/2019). The minutes print Antonio Hamilton Martins Mourão; the signed termos and decrees print Antônio.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the printed period end (31 December 2022) is prospective, no reviewed source states the day his term ended, and Alckmin's posse is not used as this end. His exercise of the Presidency on 30 and 31 December 2022 (Decrees No. 11.322 and 11.324) is claims only and never a holder or a boundary. The 28 October 2018 election, the 10 December 2018 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

holder_claims.name: Geraldo Alckmin
holder_claims.note: From 1 January 2023: declared invested as Vice-President (Geraldo José Rodrigues Alckmin Filho) for the period beginning that day, with the termo read into the record and the signed joint termo de posse at 15:00 (DCN nº 1/2023).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: the declared end (4 January 2027) is prospective and after the 7 September 2026 cutoff, and the Vice-Presidency's profile prints 31/12/2026; neither is a structured date. His exercise of the Presidency in 2026 (Laws No. 15.434 of 16 June and 15.436 of 17 June 2026) attests him as Vice-President before the cutoff but is recorded as claims only, never cited by this holder, and extends nothing. The 30 October 2022 election, the 12 December 2022 diploma and the oath are separate claims.

roles.scope_note: Vice-President of the Federative Republic of Brazil under the 1988 Constitution, recorded as an institutional office of the Presidency (the 1985 claims of BR-VP-01 are pre-period context under the earlier Constitution). CLAUDE-C01-17 keeps popular election, diplomação by the Superior Electoral Court, the oath before Congress, the declaration of posse, the termo de posse, same-session styling, styling of the incumbent before a new posse, the Vice-President's notification to exercise and exercise of the Presidency as substitute or on an interim basis, the Vice-President's succession to the Presidency, any vacancy and any stated end as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a declaration of posse or a termo de posse states that the person was invested as Vice-President for a period beginning that day, and an end only where a source states the day the vice-presidential office ended; otherwise it is dated by attested_on. No reviewed primary source states such an end or a vacancy of the Vice-Presidency, so no holder has an end and no vacancy is recorded: a successor's posse, the Vice-President's posse as President (1992, 2016), the vacancy of the office of President and periods declared at a posse are never ends. A Vice-President exercising the Presidency is recorded as claims, never as a holder of br_president or of this role, and the exercise neither splits nor ends a holder. Elections, diplomações, oaths, styling of the incumbent and a successor's tribute are never boundaries; retrospective Vice-Presidency and Presidency Library spans and chronologies are claims with no structured date. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. Twelve claims recorded by CLAUDE-C01-10 (the 1989 diplomação ceremony, the Vice-President's notification and exercise of the Presidency in 1992, 2016 and 2022 and a Presidency Library span) keep their br_president rows and are cited here; CLAUDE-C01-10's Rádio Senado news item is a lead for this role and is not cited, the notification resting on the Senate's case file (volume 48) and matter page; this role's own rows carry role_id br_vice_president. Ministers and party offices are outside this role.

unresolved: Presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-10, BR-PRES-01..10) are dated holder observations from primary Congress, Senate, Chamber, Presidency and electoral-court records. Still open: a primary record of the day José Sarney's term ended (only the Presidency Library's retrospective span gives 15 March 1990); the TSE's own minutes of the 1989-2022 diplomações; and the Diário Oficial da União originals, whose viewer requires a CAPTCHA.

Stated starts: every posse from 15 March 1990 to 1 January 2023. Stated ends: Fernando Collor de Mello (resignation, 29 December 1992) and Dilma Rousseff (Resolution No. 35, 31 August 2016) only. The ends of Itamar Franco, of each first term, of Cardoso's and Lula's second terms, of Temer and of Bolsonaro are not stated by an event record; periods declared at a posse, successors' statements, a successor's posse and 'ex-Presidente' styling are not used as ends.

Clock times: no source states the hour Collor's resignation took effect (the letter reached the Senate between 9:00 and 9:43 and was read in Congress between 11:30 and 11:50 on 29 December 1992) or the hour Rousseff received the intimation on 12 May 2016. Termo clock times differ from the session openings and are not used.

Sash transfers: only the 1 January 2019 ceremony has a Presidency record, with a misprinted dateline and no named giver; none was found for 1990, 1995, 2003, 2011, 2015 or 2023 (Senate and Chamber news-agency reports of 2003 and 2011 are leads). The Vice-President's exercise of the office (Itamar Franco from 2 October 1992, Michel Temer from 12 May 2016, Hamilton Mourão on 30-31 December 2022) is recorded only as claims.

Vice-Presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-17, BR-VP-01..10): the second role, br_vice_president, holds nine holder observations, each starting on a stated posse (Itamar Franco 15 March 1990; Marco Maciel 1995 and 1999; José Alencar 2003 and 2007; Michel Temer 2011 and 2015; Hamilton Mourão 2019; Geraldo Alckmin 2023). No reviewed primary source states the end of any vice-presidential term or a vacancy of the Vice-Presidency: not on 1 January 1990, not after Itamar Franco's posse as President on 29 December 1992 and not after Temer's on 31 August 2016 (the vacancies declared on those days are of the Presidency). Retrospective spans and the Vice-Presidency's chronology are claims only.

Still open for the Vice-Presidency: a contemporaneous record of the office on 1 January 1990 (vacant or held); the day each term ended; the hour Michel Temer began exercising the Presidency on 12 May 2016; the Vice-Presidency's own pages on gov.br (bot-check pages, not bypassed), the Diário Oficial da União (CAPTCHA) and the TSE's diplomação minutes. The Vice-President's exercise of the Presidency (1985, 1991, 1992, 2016, 2022 and 2026) is recorded only as claims.
Keep executive office distinct from party leadership; no game mapping, likeness or portrait permission is granted.

coverage.interpretation: 31 organization observations are not 31 distinct parties: 29 election-funding labels, one later registration decision and one separate PMB naming record. The reviewed HTML funding table is historical election data, not a time-frozen registry as of the research cutoff. The June 2024 aggregate announcement does not date the later release rows.
unresolved: No full Brazilian organization census or leadership timeline from 1990 through 7 September 2026 has been established.
Reconcile FEFC labels and exact process references with dated legal identities, complete names, extinct organizations, splits, mergers and name changes.
The current live registry was not used to backdate leaders or party names. A pre-cutoff archived registry snapshot remains to be obtained.
PCB and PMB release cells are dashes: no date, refusal, nonpayment, inactivity or exclusion is inferred.
The PMB article and initial notice use different names; retain the later explicit rectification and research underlying decisions before creating lifecycle intervals.
